item.title: India To Give $1.6b Aid Package To Flood-Hit Nepal
item.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi offered a $1.6 billion “development cooperation” package to neighbouring Nepal on Monday in the wake of devastating Himalayan floods. “We express our deep condolences for the loss of lives caused by the devastating floods in Nepal in August,” Modi said, standing alongside his Nepali counterpart Balendra Shah in New Delhi. “To support Nepal’s reconstruction, and give fresh momentum to its long-term development, we announce a development cooperation package worth 240 billion Nepali rupees ($1.6 billion),” he said. India did not immediately give specific details of what the development package included. Shah was given a military honour guard parade at the presidential palace in New Delhi, on his first trip to a neighbouring country since taking office in March. Rescuers use an excavator to transport a flood survivor following flash floods and a landslide at Devighat in Nepal’s Nuwakot district on August 26, 2026. Photo by PRAKASH MATHEMA / AFP The rapper-turned-politician came to power following a wave of youth-led anti-corruption protests in September 2025. Shah, 36, wearing his trademark sunglasses and dressed in black, was given a bear hug by Modi, 76, dressed all in white. Unlike his predecessors, Shah had initially refrained from foreign visits since becoming prime minister. His first overseas trip was to New York in September, where he addressed the United Nations General Assembly as Nepal reeled from a deadly tsunami-like flood, triggered by a high-altitude glacial mountain collapse, that killed more than 1,400 people and left 5,000 missing. ‘Deal with future disasters’ A man looks at the remains in the aftermath of flash floods at Trishuli in Nepal’s Nuwakot district on September 7, 2026. Photo by PEDRO PARDO / AFP Nepal, a largely rural country that contributes little to global greenhouse gas emissions, estimates reconstruction will cost $4.78 billion. Shah said it showed the “imperative to address the challenges of climate change through collective action”. In October, the United Nations’ climate loss and damage fund agreed the modest sum of $20 million in aid to Nepal — the maximum amount countries can request in a single application — and the first time it has set aside money for any country. Nepal, a landlocked Himalayan nation of 30 million people, has long had to balance its relations with its two giant neighbours, India and China. “Our commitment will be to help affected families rebuild their lives, create new opportunities and further strengthen Nepal’s capacity to deal with future disasters,” Modi said. An aerial view shows a torrent of muddy water surging past houses and through the Trishuli river in the aftermath of flash floods, at Betrawati in Nepal’s Nuwakot district on August 29, 2026. item.title: Eisenkot, Netanyahu parties to meet again for Israel coalition talks
item.description: The parties of caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Gadi Eisenkot, who is tasked with forming the next Israeli government, are due to resume coalition talks on Monday after negotiations a day earlier delivered no agreement. The third round of talks comes as Eisenkot’s wide-ranging camp faces divisions on whether to forge alliances with the ultra-Orthodox parties, or the Arab-majority lists, or whether to form a national unity government with Netanyahu’s Likud. Former military chief Eisenkot has until December 6 — a deadline which can be extended by 14 days — to form a government to replace Netanyahu after the October election failed to deliver a clear majority for either bloc. Delegations from Eisenkot’s centrist Yashar party and Netanyahu’s right-wing Likud are due to meet on Monday evening for a third round of negotiations, a spokesperson for Likud told AFP. Representatives from each party met for nearly four hours on Sunday and laid out their positions “on a range of substantive issues,” with no sign of a breakthrough. – Political ‘boycotts’ – On Saturday, Yashar presented the talks as “a genuine commitment to forming the broadest possible government”, saying that Eisenkot had asked his representatives to explore all options. Likud immediately laid down several conditions for its participation in a unity government, including an end to “all personal attacks” and political “boycotts” targeting Netanyahu and his government. Eisenkot’s 48-member bloc needs 61 lawmakers to reach a majority and remains divided over how to build a coalition. Short of 61 lawmakers, Eisenkot’s bloc could form a minority government. The head of the left-leaning Democrats party, Yair Golan, on Monday called for an end to the “sham talks with Likud”. Netanyahu is pushing for a national unity government, which could see a rotation of the premiership between the two men, a mechanism already tried in Israel. Such an arrangement could allow Netanyahu to keep his political leverage against the corruption charges he faces, as well as continue to oppose the creation of an independent commission of inquiry into the security failures that preceded the Hamas attack of October 7, 2023. But that prospect runs up against Eisenkot’s refusal to serve in a cabinet led by Netanyahu, against whom he centred his campaign. Last week, Eisenkot said that he would be prepared to put forward a minority national emergency government for a parliamentary vote should efforts to create a broad-based government fail. The post Eisenkot, Netanyahu parties to meet again for Israel coalition talks appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Airbus may be leaving Microsoft Office, but for its 36,000 defense staff, Office isn't leaving them
item.description: Airbus has a plan to phase out Microsoft Office, but about 22 percent of its roughly 165,000 employees will stay on it because their sensitive data must remain on-premise. In March 2018, Airbus signed a contract with Google to move its workforce - 130,000 strong at that time - onto the cloud-based Workspace suite. Years later, compatibility issues mean some users still need Excel. Catherine Jestin, Airbus's executive vice president of digital, told The Register that Google is still working to resolve software interface conflicts between departments and improve features. Last year, for example, Google tripled the number of cells available in Sheets, which let Airbus "reduce significantly the number of users on Microsoft." This year, Google improved the compatibility of document watermarking. Contracts, for instance, are often exported from Excel to Sheets by one department, edited by another, and sent back. "Sometimes we had compatibility issues when you were commenting, the comments were lost, or they were not transferable in one way or the other," she said. "Now they [Google] have made it totally compatible, which means that it makes it much easier for us to decommission people working on contracts… the legal department, the sales department, purchasing department, making it much easier to have that internal collaboration." Airbus and Google have a roadmap to eliminate Microsoft Office. Jestin expects the migration to finish in "another two to three years." Not every part of the company will switch. The Defence division , which accounts for the 22 percent (more than 36,000 people), will keep using classic Microsoft Office. "We will not get 100 percent out of Microsoft because again, for the defense industry people, they cannot [use] Microsoft Office 365 or Google Workspace, they have to stay on-premise, and the only solution that is available on-premise is Microsoft. So Microsoft Office will remain for colleagues who are working in the defense and space programs." As we pointed out a year ago, kicking the Microsoft habit is no easy feat. ®

item.title: Bad COP, Worse COP: What’s Next After Climate Talks Fail?
item.description: The collapse of marathon climate talks in Turkey has renewed questions about reform of their consensus requirement, and galvanised calls for legal action and ambitious side agreements between like-minded countries. The “conference of the parties” talks, better known as COP31, ended without agreement and two days over schedule on Sunday, as countries deadlocked on fossil fuels, finance, science and carbon-removing technologies. It was an ignominious end for an unusual dual-presidency shared by Australia and Turkey, and negotiations chair Chris Bowen, who is Australia’s climate minister, said it was “very disappointing”. For many observers, the outcome was the inevitable result of a process that has regularly been hamstrung by its insistence on consensus. “Decision-making that requires every country to agree on every comma is not fit for a climate emergency,” said Nikki Reisch, director of the Center of International Environmental Law’s climate and energy programme. Bowen identified the same issue. “The fundamental root of the problem is that when COP was created, for reasons I understand, it was made consensus only,” he said. “That’s a very tough ask.” ‘Significant reform’ COP31 President and Turkey’s Minister of Environment, Urbanisation and Climate Change Murat Kurum (C) attends a plenary session of the United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) at the Antalya Expo Centre, in Antalya on November 22, 2026. Sunday’s collapse has renewed calls for a reform to that consensus-based process, in which any one country, or a small minority, can nix progress. “It has been clear for years that the COP process is in need of significant reform,” wrote former US vice president Al Gore on X. He urged a “reinvigorated multilateral process that reflects the latest science and represents the will of the majority of the world.” But as Bowen noted, “you also need consensus to change consensus” — in other words, all countries would have to agree those reforms. He described that as a “particular challenge,” although others might characterise it as simply impossible. The COP31 talks deadlocked over multiple issues, notably whether the so-called cover decision would mention phasing out planet-warming fossil fuels. Several countries refused a deal without that mention, while others including Saudi Arabia were vehemently opposed to its inclusion. There were other serious faultlines, including the timing of scientific work from the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, and language on carbon capture, a technology championed by the fossil fuel industry but criticised by some as costly and ineffective. Crucially for developing countries, there was also no progress on finance — the money badly needed to help countries transition energy systems and adapt to the natural disasters climate change is already worsening. “The fundamental problem for globally agreed climate policy is more starkly obvious than ever: fossil fuel powers will not agree to have their resource

item.title: Solape Fayemi Launches Saina Properties Across Four Markets
item.description: For many people, buying property is one of the biggest financial decisions they will ever make. Yet, knowing who to trust, how to verify ownership and whether a property is worth the investment can make the process overwhelming. It is a challenge Solape Fayemi hopes to address with the launch of Saina Properties , a real estate company now operating across Nigeria, the United Kingdom, the United States and the United Arab Emirates. Officially unveiled at an event held on 17 November at the Marriott Hotel, Ikeja GRA, Lagos, Saina Properties is built around a simple idea: property ownership should be guided by sound advice, proper verification and professional support, not just the excitement of closing a deal. For Solape, whose experience in the investment industry shaped her understanding of money, risk and wealth creation, the decision to establish the company came from recognising the need for a more considered approach to real estate. “We are not building Saina Properties because the world needs another company selling properties. We are building Saina because we believe there is room for a different kind of real estate experience. One where advice comes before the transaction, where due diligence is not treated as an inconvenience, and where people are encouraged to ask questions, understand their options and make informed decisions,” she said at the launch. That philosophy is reflected in the company’s three core areas of expertise: Advisory & Verification, Sales & Brokerage, and Developments . Rather than focusing solely on connecting buyers to properties, Saina brings together the guidance investors need to assess opportunities, the support required to navigate property transactions, and involvement in real estate development. The company is also building on experience gained before its official launch, having supported more than 25 clients with property opportunities across different markets. An important part of its proposition is the role of professional expertise in protecting property investors. Fayemi’s position raises a familiar question: people consult doctors for medical concerns and lawyers for legal matters, so why do some investors leave significant property decisions in the hands of relatives simply because they are available or familiar with the location? While trust and family relationships matter, they do not automatically translate into the technical knowledge needed to assess a property, verify its documentation or understand its investment potential. These decisions require proper checks, market understanding and accountability. With its operations spanning four markets, Saina Properties aims to support individuals and investors looking to navigate property ownership with greater clarity, whether they are buying, selling or exploring development opportunities. item.title: Nigeria not ready to host World Cup, says FIFA president
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde FIFA President Gianni Infantino has said Nigeria is not currently ready to host the FIFA World Cup, citing the need for investment in stadiums, hotels, airports and transportation infrastructure. Infantino made this known in an interview with Arise News, aired on Monday, while responding to a question on what it would take for a country like Nigeria to host the global football tournament. “The key for hosting a World Cup is the infrastructure: the stadiums, hotels, airports, and transportation. This is where the investment is really necessary. “A country like Nigeria has the resources, the passion, and the will as well,” he said. Asked directly whether Nigeria was ready to host the World Cup, Infantino replied, “Today, no, but tomorrow, why not?” Nigeria last hosted a FIFA tournament in 2009, when it staged the FIFA U-17 World Cup, with Switzerland defeating Nigeria’s Golden Eaglets 1-0 in the final in Abuja. On his 10-year tenure as FIFA president, Infantino said the organisation’s growth and the expansion of its competitions reflected the work done under his leadership. “I think the facts really speak quite loudly here. Speak for themselves. The organisation of the World Cups, both for men and women, increasing the number of teams, increasing the competitive balance of these competitions, and the revenue news. “Of course, we moved from a bit more than 5 billion before I arrived to 16 billion in this last cycle,” he said. He added that football and FIFA had continued to grow, saying such progress required hard work and strict compliance with established standards. “Football is growing. FIFA is growing. This is not possible if you don’t work hard, but also if you don’t work in compliance with the highest possible standard,” he said. Infantino was in Nigeria over the weekend, where on Friday, he inspected the remodelled Warri City Stadium alongside FIFA Secretary-General Mattias Grafström. During the visit, h e praised Nigeria’s football heritage and the country’s contribution to the global game , noting that some of the world’s finest players came from Nigeria, particularly Delta State. “This stadium is fantastic. It has everything you can dream of. I just would love to wear some shorts and kick the ball. So as soon as it’s completely finished, we’d come and play games with all these great Nigerian legends who come from this region. “Not just in Nigeria, but some of the best players in the world come from Nigeria, come from Delta State,” he said. At the 48th Ordinary General Assembly of the Confederation of African Football in Abuja, on Saturday, Infantino also commended President Bola Tinubu for investments in sports facilities, saying they demonstrated the country’s commitment to its young population. “He is doing, together with all of you, fantastic job here in Nigeria, showing that you are a country projected into the future,” he said. He added, “The investments done in sports facilities, infrastructure, show that you beli

item.title: Nothing will stop 750km Coastal Highway – Umahi
item.description: By John Alechenu, Abuja The Minister of Works, Senator David Umahi, has reaffirmed President Bola Tinubu’s commitment to completing the 750-kilometre Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, declaring that nothing will stop the project. Umahi spoke during an inspection of bridges on Sections 1 and 2 of the highway. The disclosure was made in a statement by Francis Nwaze, Senior Special Assistant to the Minister, in Abuja on Monday. He quoted the minister as saying, “Nothing will happen to the 750-kilometre Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, which passes through the nine coastal states. The President has directed that the project must be completed as envisaged.” Umahi described the highway as a profitable national investment capable of generating revenue, attracting private investors and unlocking tourism and industrial opportunities. “We are using concrete, and so we are entitled to carbon credits claim. We are also using solar instead of conventional electricity; we are entitled to carbon credits,” he said. He added that the superhighway would accommodate tourism facilities, factories, CCTV surveillance and other commercial infrastructure, with private investors already showing interest in recovering costs through investment arrangements. The minister disclosed that President Tinubu is expected to commission Section 1 this month or early December. He also clarified that the reconstruction of the East-West Road is an additional commitment by the President and does not replace or affect the Coastal Highway. He described the ongoing 1,068-kilometre Sokoto-Badagry Road as another major infrastructure undertaking of the administration, stressing that Tinubu is pursuing multiple major projects simultaneously. Umahi commended the President for the scale of infrastructure development and economic reforms, citing declining inflation, improved foreign exchange access for businesses and the absence of ASUU strikes. He urged Nigerians, particularly South-East residents in Lagos, to support the President, noting that the administration has delivered significant infrastructure projects to the region. Meanwhile, Umahi has ordered a three-week nationwide emergency rehabilitation of major federal highways ahead of the festive season and the January 2027 elections. He directed Zonal Directors, Controllers, Resident Engineers and contractors to return to the field immediately to ensure critical roads are made motorable across all six geopolitical zones. “I feel so sad that a contractor will be on site doing permanent work, yet some sections of the roads remain impassable. This practice must stop,” he said. He warned that contractors must not allow motorists to suffer on failed sections while permanent construction continues, directing that damaged portions be excavated and rehabilitated using appropriate materials and asphalt where necessary. item.title: When Microsoft, Apple, and the FAA can't keep it up, it's a system of a down
item.description: No Access November is going well this year. Among the many organizations to adopt Outage As A Service (OAAS) were Microsoft , Apple , the FAA , and any number of European supermarkets . Even the NSA has succumbed. For us, at least, outage is word of the year. It's certainly deeply embedded in the public mind, with schoolchildren reportedly referring to the 19th century Irish famine as "the potato outage." There's no danger of an outrage outage. OAAS is synonymous with infrastructure failure, a more useful term that begins to hint at cause and cure as well as effect. In all of the latest crop, what we know is depressingly familiar. Microsoft's O365 meltdown was a cascading failure caused by a botched upgrade that took stuff offline and melted down as it tried to come back. The FAA was a migration from Jurassic hardware that wasn't end of life so much as living fossil. The Eurofridge-cum-fondue-maker was a control system so badly written it fell apart if you raised an eyebrow at it. Clearly, nobody had. Until now. These are all different classes of OAAS that have been around for decades. Security-based outages are still outages, and a packet flood is still a packet flood whether it's a botnet DDoS or finger trouble in the config dashboard. Each of them has a root cause with obvious fixes – a faulty mental model of network/server interaction, chronic underfunding, a complete supply chain with little cyber-security expertise. All these, like the poor, will be with us always. They won't fix themselves. Infrastructure that works is invisible, and invisible things are forgotten until they break. What's needed is an infrastructure that watches itself, that is designed to be adaptive and resilient, one that refuses to connect to danger and nulls out any that gets through. There have been attempts to create a ground-up architecture that is inherently risk resistant. One such is SCION (Scalability, Control, and Isolation On Next-generation networks). It redesigns routing between domains around explicit path selection, separate control and data planes, and mechanisms for trust and failure isolation. The result is a very resilient, very reliable, and very secure infrastructure that reflects the designers' tenet that you can't patch the internet into any of these things. Start from scratch or GTFO. SCION started about 15 years ago, and it works well enough to be adopted by entities like the Secure Swiss Finance Network . If the Gnomes of Zurich trust it, no higher accreditation exists. Well, it was designed by ETH Zürich. Where you won't find it is almost everywhere else. The internet is like Switzerland in the same way the Amazon rainforest is like Central Park. There are trees and sometimes it rains. It is unwise to infer anything else. Given you can't manicure existing infrastructure into true resilience, the only other option is evolution. A couple of billion years of continued life on Earth has proved this is the only way to re-engineer complex systems wh

item.title: Democrats win largest US House majority since 1992
item.description: Democrats have won the largest majority in the US House of Representatives in more than three decades, after Chuck Hubbard defeated Republican representative Virginia Foxx in North Carolina, US media projected on Sunday. The party won full control of both the House and Senate in a sweeping midterm rout with a landslide of upsets that delivered a crushing rebuke of President Donald Trump and his Republican Party. CBS News and NBC News projected Hubbard’s win on Sunday, securing the Democrats a 258th seat in Congress’ 435-member House. The majority is the largest won by either party since 1992, when Bill Clinton won the presidency and Democrats won a total of 258 seats. “House Democrats have just secured the largest majority any party in Congress has held this century. BOOM,” House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries said in a post on X. Sunday’s result came after Foxx requested a recount. Hubbard said Sunday that he had spoken with Foxx, who “graciously conceded following the results of the recount process.” “Let me be the first to thank Congresswoman Foxx for her decades of service and countless sacrifices,” he added on X. The Democratic victory hands the party the power to block Trump’s agenda and investigate alleged corruption for the last two years of his presidency. The midterm results reflected deep anger over living costs, tariffs and Trump’s war against Iran, which has sent fuel prices soaring and compounded dissatisfaction with an already deeply unpopular president. item.title: How Mary Akinwola Graduated with a Distinction from Oxford After Receiving Multiple Scholarships
item.description: Mary Akinwola graduated from the University of Oxford after receiving the Chevening and Mastercard Foundation Scholarships. My name is Mary Akinwola. I’m a physiotherapist, a strategy consultant, a healthcare entrepreneur, and I recently graduated from the University of Oxford with a distinction in Health Service Improvement and Evaluation. I have probably said that last part a hundred times since getting my results, and honestly, I don’t think I’m tired of saying it yet. Haha! One thing about me is that I like to be involved. I am sometimes curious about things that have absolutely nothing to do with what I’m supposed to be doing, and I genuinely enjoy working with people. I like organising things, bringing people together, and seeing an idea move forward to get accomplished. So I have known that going to Oxford was never going to be just about getting a master’s degree. Let me explain how I ended up there. I studied Physiotherapy at the University of Ibadan, where I graduated with First-Class Honours. During my undergraduate years, I was involved in quite a lot outside academics: student leadership, journalism, research, community health programmes and advocacy. My involvement in community health exposed me to how differently people experience healthcare depending on where they live, what they can afford and what information they have access to. I loved being a physiotherapist, and that allowed me to interrogate questions that went beyond individual patient care. Why do some people receive good healthcare while others struggle to access even basic services? How do we make healthcare more affordable? What role can technology play? And why do some seemingly good healthcare programmes struggle to produce lasting change? Eventually, I realised I wanted to study and work in a field that constantly seeks to improve health systems. I researched different programmes across the US and UK, hoping to study at institutions that have international audiences where I could build a diverse perspective in health. I came across the MSc in Health Service Improvement and Evaluation at the University of Oxford’s Nuffield Department of Medicine. It aligned with many of my interests, so I applied. I also needed a scholarship because, quite frankly, I couldn’t afford Oxford. It was a humbling and affirming process. I was awarded scholarships such as the Chevening Scholarship and two Oxford-based scholarships. I still feel fortunate to have received and chosen the Mastercard Foundation-Africa Oxford Initiative Scholarship, which fully funded my studies. I am deeply grateful for that opportunity. Now, I think it’s important to say that I was very excited about the academic programme. I wanted to understand healthcare systems better, learn new research methods and become more effective at designing and evaluating healthcare services. However, I was also very excited about everything else. I was going to be at Oxford! There were going to be people from different countries

item.title: African players in Europe: Mixed fortunes for Nigerian Awoniyi
item.description: Nigerian Taiwo Awoniyi scored for Coventry City and later had to be substituted after collapsing in a Premier League victory over Crystal Palace at the weekend. AFP Sport highlights African headline-makers in the major European leagues: ENGLAND TAIWO AWONIYI (Coventry City) The striker scored his third goal for Coventry in a 3-2 win against bottom club Palace, but his afternoon came to a bizarre premature end. Awoniyi netted in the fifth minute with a close-range finish into the far corner from Jack Rudoni’s pass to put Coventry 1-0 up at the CBS Arena. But the 29-year-old, signed from Nottingham Forest in the close season, was forced to miss the last 45 minutes after going down clutching his leg in pain while the players were lining up to start the second half. Awoniyi had to be helped up off the ground by two Palace players and limped off, forcing bemused Coventry boss Frank Lampard to make an unexpected substitution. Lampard admitted afterwards that Awoniyi felt a slight problem with his ankle from the first half. SPAIN YASSIR ZABIRI (Racing Santander) Moroccan forward Zabiri struck twice in the opening stages to help Santander beat Real Sociedad 3-2 in La Liga. The 21-year-old, on loan from Rennes, climbed to 11 league goals and trails only Raphinha and Kylian Mbappe in the Spanish scoring charts. Zabiri smashed home in the sixth minute for the opener and two minutes later was alert to pinch the ball from Real Sociedad’s goalkeeper and roll it into the empty net for his second. GERMANY JUMA BAH (Augsburg) Sierra Leone and Augsburg centre-back Bah netted his first goal since arriving on a season-long loan from Manchester City in his side’s 3-1 home romp over Mainz in the Bundesliga. With Augsburg 1-0 up, Bah was on the spot to prod a loose ball across the line from a corner to give the hosts their second. FRANCE PATRICK ZABI (Paris FC) Ivorian Zabi opened the scoring just after half-time as second-placed Paris FC hammered lowly visitors Angers 4-0 to lie second in Ligue 1 after 11 rounds, three points behind European champions Paris Saint-Germain. A cross was nodded into the path of the 20-year-old, and he slammed the ball into the net. BOULAYE DIA (Lorient) Dia, a 2022 Africa Cup of Nations champion with Senegal, put Lorient ahead away to Rennes in a 1-1 draw between mid-table clubs. Tunisian Montassar Talbi equalised in the final minute of the first half. The post African players in Europe: Mixed fortunes for Nigerian Awoniyi appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: Tinubu won’t be included in my national unity govt — Makinde
item.description: The presidential candidate of the Action Peoples Movement (APM), Seyi Makinde, has ruled out including President Bola Tinubu in his proposed government of national unity if elected in 2027, accusing the president of failing to honour an agreement they reached ahead of the 2023 election. Makinde, however, said he would consider appointing capable members of the All Progressives Congress (APC) into his government, insisting that there were decent people in the ruling party who could contribute to governance. He stated this during an interview on The Rooftop Podcast, where he was asked whether he would bring former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, Peter Obi and Tinubu into his government if elected. “Perhaps not President Tinubu, but there are still decent people in APC as well. I’ll tap them and they are Nigerians,” Makinde said. Asked whether he did not consider Tinubu decent, the governor said his position was informed by his experience working with the president during the 2023 election, when an agreement on a government of national unity was allegedly reached but not fulfilled. “Well, not in that context. I mean, I worked for him in 2023. We agreed on a government of national unity. He did not fulfil it,” he said. Makinde explained that the agreement was part of the position taken by the PDP G5 governors, who broke ranks with the party’s leadership ahead of the 2023 presidential election, saying they wanted an inclusive government that would draw competent Nigerians from across the country, irrespective of political affiliation. “We came from the PDP as G5 and we said, ‘Look, this is not going to be a government of APC. It should be a government where you tap people from all across the country. Go to every corner of the country, pick and choose people that can help you know to sort some of this out,’” he said. The APM candidate said the idea of a government of national unity was not new, citing the administration of the late military Head of State, General Sani Abacha, as an example of efforts to bring prominent Nigerians into government to ease political tensions. He recalled that following the annulment of the June 12, 1993 presidential election, Abacha appointed prominent figures, including former Lagos State governor Lateef Jakande and businessman Alex Ibru, to his government. Makinde said the appointments were intended to calm tensions and pacify aggrieved Nigerians. “And it’s been done before. After the annulment of the June 12, 1993 elections, and General Abacha came into government, they went and tapped Alhaji Jakande, Alex Ibru, all of those were geared towards bringing down the temperature in the country and ensuring that where there are angry people, they are being pacified,” he said. He accused Tinubu of failing to replicate such an inclusive approach, alleging that the president’s appointments were largely drawn from his political circle. “Tinubu didn’t do that at all. item.title: Software issues have even reached Mercury as BepiColombo probe arrives in uncertain state
item.description: Humanity’s third-ever mission to Mercury has arrived, but a last-minute “software issue” has complicated matters. The BepiColombo mission is a joint effort by the European Space Agency (ESA) and Japan’s Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA). Reaching Mercury is not easy because its gravity is weak and its orbit is fast. The tiny planet’s proximity to the Sun further complicates matters, because our star’s gravity accelerates everything that falls towards it. BepiColombo’s journey has therefore seen it whiz past Earth once, Venus twice, and Mercury six times on a complicated path the two space agencies designed to slow it down sufficiently to be captured by mercurial gravity, while also keeping up with its rapid orbit. In 2024, the craft’s thrusters underperformed, leading the ESA and JAXA to re-plot the planned trajectory and reschedule its arrival at Mercury from mid-2025 to this past weekend. The ESA’s operations team sent the commands to insert BepiColombo into orbit on Friday. On Sunday the craft phoned home with news that it entered orbit. A little later, however, the ESA revealed “the thruster burn was shorter than planned following a software issue.” The spacecraft is safe, but the ESA says it is “working to understand what happened” and promised updates early this week. Readers may recall that a pair of NASA missions to Mars are also experiencing software glitches , which have in recent weeks become all-too-prevalent on Earth, too. Fingers crossed If all is well, BepiColombo will deploy two orbiters. The ESA’s craft is called the Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO), which the ESA says will map the planet, assess the composition of its surface and interior, measure its magnetic field, and even gather data that scientists hope will “test Einstein's theory of General Relativity to an unprecedented level of accuracy.” JAXA’s Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MIO) will also investigate the planet’s magnetic field, plasma, dust, and atmosphere. Both orbiters are extraordinary feats of engineering. As JAXA explains , MIO is solar-powered but the sunlight it will receive at Mercury is around ten times as powerful as on Earth. Mercury itself is also sufficiently hot that the orbiter needs protection from heat radiated from the planet’s surface. ESA’s MPO keeps itself cool with three to four insulating blankets comprised of layered titanium, aluminum, and a ceramic fabric called Nextel. The blankets alone weigh 94kg. The two space agencies expect to start science operations in April 2027 but haven’t yet said if the two orbiters are in peak condition. JAXA, sadly, last week revealed that its Hayabusa2 probe has deteriorated to the point at which it can no longer make its planned landing on asteroid 1998 KY26. JAXA scheduled that for the year 2031, but problems with the probe’s thrusters mean the agency will instead attempt a high-speed fly-by of asteroid 2015 BM510 in 2028. Hayabusa2 launched in 2014, so is rather older than BepiColombo. Humanity has visite

item.title: Tourist accuses Daura Emir of sexual assault
item.description: The Emir of Daura, His Royal Highness Alhaji Faruq Umar-Faruk, has been embroiled in an alleged sexual assault of a foreign tourist who visited his palace in Daura, Katsina State, during her tour of Nigeria. The tourist, who identified herself on Instagram as @beduinqa, alleged in a viral video that the 92-year-old monarch fondled her hand and other body parts. The video has elicited reactions, with Amnesty International Nigeria and prominent voices in the North calling for a thorough probe into the act. When contacted, the Daura Emirate spokesperson (Sarkin Labarai), Ibrahim Murtala, confirmed that the Emirate has seen the video and they are currently analyzing its content, adding that the Emirate will address the matter after the conclusion of the ongoing processes. He did not respond to a text message sent to him either. The Katsina State Police Public Relations Officer (PPRO), Abubakar Sadiq Aliyu, said the command was not aware of the video and did not receive any formal complaint from anyone on the matter. Describing the alleged experience, the tourist said she found it disgusting and had continued to think about what happened. She explained that although the incident occurred on November 14, she chose not to make it public until she had completed her tour and left the country. In a post shared on her Instagram page alongside the video, the tourist wrote: “Recently I finished 30 days journey exploring all around #Nigeria. I had amazing time, saw beautiful places, met great people. “Unfortunately I had also a bad experience when visiting #daura in Northern Nigeria. During visit to the #emirofdaura palace I was taken to an elegant room where we sat on a couch and started talking. It was strange for me that he grabbed my hand and started playing with it. “Then when we stood up, he hugged me, kissed my cheek (which was also surprising for me), and then he grabbed my boobs. item.title: 2027: Why Nigerians should prefer me to Obi-Kwankwaso – Makinde
item.description: By Bayo Wahab Oyo State Governor and Allied Peoples Movement (APM) presidential candidate, Seyi Makinde, has explained why Nigerians should choose his ticket with former Kano State governor, Ibrahim Shekarau’s associate Daura, over the Peter Obi-Rabiu Kwankwaso ticket in the 2027 presidential election. Makinde cited the historic alliance between the Southwest and North, his experience in governance, youthful energy and plans for national unity as key advantages of his candidacy. Speaking on The Rooftop Podcast, the governor said the relationship between the two regions had helped Nigeria maintain stability during difficult periods, arguing that his ticket was positioned to sustain that tradition. “Apart from the traditional Southwest-North alliance, because that alliance has always provided stability for Nigeria in time of crisis in the past,” Makinde said. He recalled Nigeria’s first military coup, arguing that the Southwest and North had historically played significant roles in efforts to preserve the country’s stability. “If you even go back to the first military coup in Nigeria, the people that were wasted were basically the north and southwest, because we’re always in the forefront of stability for the country, and that is what we have brought to the table,” he said. Makinde also pointed to his performance in Oyo State and what he described as the youthful energy of his ticket, saying his administration’s achievements and commitments could be measured against documented promises. He said his political agenda was designed to allow Nigerians hold him accountable for his promises, rather than rely solely on campaign rhetoric. The APM candidate also outlined his proposed transitional government of national unity, saying it would address Nigeria’s political and security challenges through a broader national consensus. Makinde said he was willing to lead such a transition but would not remain in office to benefit from its eventual outcome, arguing that doing so could compromise his decisions. “I can lead it, but I will not be a beneficiary of the outcome because if I’m looking at myself benefiting from that outcome, it may cloud my judgment and also block how I will take that decision,” he said. He said the proposed arrangement was necessary because insecurity and other problems affecting Nigeria were not confined to any particular region. “And a government of national unity, because, you know, you look at insecurity and things fueling it all around the country. It’s not limited to any area,” Makinde said. The post 2027: Why Nigerians should prefer me to Obi-Kwankwaso – Makinde appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Kwankwaso broke APC defection pact with Tinubu — Abba
item.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo Kano State Governor, Abba Kabir Yusuf, has accused his former political mentor, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, of reneging on an agreement to defect to the All Progressives Congress (APC) after the 2023 governorship election. Yusuf, who made the allegation in an interview with BBC Hausa, said Kwankwaso personally asked him to approach President Bola Tinubu and assure him that they would join the APC if the President did not interfere in the legal battle over the Kano governorship election. The governor said the agreement was reached after the 2023 election, when his victory over the APC candidate, Nasiru Yusuf Gawuna, was being challenged in court. According to Yusuf, Kwankwaso initiated the arrangement and asked him to swear by the Holy Qur’an that they would return to the APC if the judicial process was allowed to run its course without interference. “Kwankwaso himself sent me to Tinubu and asked me to tell him that we had made that promise. He even wanted me to swear by the Holy Qur’an that if God granted us victory, we would all come together,” Yusuf told the BBC. He said he honoured the agreement and subsequently assured Tinubu of their intention to defect. Yusuf added that Kwankwaso also held several meetings with the President and sent delegations to discuss the proposed political realignment. The governor, who formally defected from the New Nigeria Peoples Party (NNPP) to the APC on January 26, 2026, insisted that he did not betray his former political benefactor but fulfilled an agreement that Kwankwaso later abandoned. He also dismissed suggestions that his defection was a political arrangement aimed at weakening the opposition or distracting the public, maintaining that Kwankwaso was aware of the discussions and arrangements leading to the move. Yusuf, however, said some remarks allegedly made by Kwankwaso shortly after he had assured Tinubu of their planned defection undermined the arrangement. He said the comments were communicated to the President and reportedly did not go down well with him. On his relationship with Kwankwaso since their political separation, Yusuf said they had occasionally communicated, adding that he sometimes sent messages to greet his former mentor. He declined to discuss publicly allegations that Kwankwaso had exerted undue influence over his administration or prevented him from exercising his responsibilities as governor, saying such matters were better left outside the media. Marital crisis The governor also spoke about the reported marital crisis between him and his wife, Zainab Musa Kwankwaso, a niece of the former Kano governor. Yusuf said their marriage, which began about 20 years ago, produced children, but difficulties eventually emerged in their relationship. He alleged that his wife’s belongings were removed from his residence and that she was taken away without his knowledge. item.title: Techie turned his too-easy job interview into a trap
item.description: Returning to work after the weekend can feel like voluntarily walking into a trap. To help readers feel a little freer, The Register therefore uses Monday mornings to serve up a new installment of " Who, Me? " It's the column in which we share your stories of mistakes, misjudgments, and occasional misanthropy. This week, meet a reader we'll Regomize as "Marshall," who told us about a job interview he endured about 20 years ago. The interview included a practical component he described as "Here's a PC, we've broken a few things in it, get it going." Marshall quickly spotted some mundane faults, such as a loose PCI card and unplugged internal cables. He felt the test was too easy. "One of the things I always checked was whether the power supply 110/230 switch was set for the UK," he told The Register . Getting the PC running earned Marshall a job offer, but he couldn't resist suggesting a tougher test. "I said to my future manager: 'Would it be a good thing to set the power supply to the wrong voltage as part of the interview test?' He said that wasn't fair." Marshall stayed in the job for two years. A couple of months after he left, his former manager sent him a short email. "Ha-ha, very funny." Marshall asked another former colleague what might have prompted that email. "It turned out somebody – I don't know if it was an interview candidate – had blown a power supply by not checking the voltage it was set to." What a coincidence! Or maybe not? "It wasn't anything to do with me," Marshall insisted. "No idea who it was." Have you held colleagues to a higher standard than the boss expected? Or left a little trap for them to trip over? In either case, click here to send email to Who, Me? We appreciate the chance to share your stories, and do so with appropriate anonymization so that contributors never step into the jaws of trouble. ®

item.title: Senate committee hails Air Peace over ₦80,000 military fare
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Senate Committee on Army has commended Air Peace and its Chairman, Dr Allen Onyema, for introducing a discounted one-way domestic air fare of ₦80,000 for serving and retired personnel of the Nigerian Armed Forces. The committee also urged other airlines and corporate organisations in the country to emulate the gesture as part of efforts to improve the welfare of military personnel and veterans. The commendation was contained in a statement issued on Sunday by the Chairman of the committee, Senator Abdulaziz Musa Yar’Adua, representing Katsina Central Senatorial District. According to the statement, the initiative was unveiled on November 16, 2026, during the 2026 Chief of Defence Intelligence Annual Conference in Abuja. The committee said the discounted fare was available to eligible military personnel who had served in the Nigerian Armed Forces since 1960, across all domestic routes. It added that Air Peace would also bear the cost of tickets for regional and international flights, with beneficiaries required to pay only applicable taxes and charges. Describing the initiative as a patriotic gesture, the committee said it was a practical demonstration of appreciation for the sacrifices made by serving and retired military personnel in defending the country’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. It noted that members of the Armed Forces had continued to make enormous sacrifices, often at great personal cost, and deserved tangible support that would improve their welfare and that of their families. “By reducing the burden of air travel, Air Peace has demonstrated that patriotism is not only spoken in times of ceremony, but shown in practical action that touches the lives of those who serve,” the statement said. The committee particularly praised Onyema for what it described as his consistent commitment to humanitarian causes, national development and support for the Nigerian military. It also endorsed the airline chairman’s call for the military leadership to establish a robust verification system to ensure that only genuine beneficiaries access the concession. According to the committee, such a mechanism would help make the initiative sustainable, transparent and free from abuse. It appealed to other airlines and corporate organisations to support the Armed Forces, describing the welfare of serving personnel and veterans as a collective national responsibility. “The private sector has a critical role to play in complementing the efforts of the Federal Government in improving the welfare and morale of our troops and veterans,” it said. The Senate committee assured Air Peace of its support and readiness to work with the airline, the Ministry of Defence and the Service Chiefs to ensure the smooth implementation of the initiative. It reiterated its appreciation to the airline’s management for the gesture, describing it as a meaningful tribute to Nigeria’s military personnel. The post Senate committee hails Air Peace over ₦

item.title: FG partners world’s largest pivot irrigation maker
item.description: By Favour Ulebor The Federal Government has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Valmont Industries Inc., the world’s largest manufacturer of pivot irrigation systems, to accelerate the implementation of its flagship Irrigate Nigeria Programme. The agreement also provides for the establishment of an irrigation equipment production plant in Nigeria in partnership with the National Agency for Science and Engineering Infrastructure (NASENI), as part of efforts to boost local manufacturing and reduce dependence on imported irrigation technology. The Presidential Implementation Committee on Technology Transfer (PICTT) signed the agreement with Valmont at the weekend. In a statement issued by NASENI on Sunday, the Chairman of PICTT, Dr Dahiru Muhammed, who is also coordinating the implementation of the Irrigate Nigeria Programme, said the agreement formally brought Valmont, through its Valley Irrigation brand, on board as a major partner in developing irrigation infrastructure across the country. Muhammed, who signed the agreement alongside Valmont’s Regional Vice President for the Middle East and Africa, Mr Kalle Autto, described the partnership as a significant step towards expanding mechanised irrigation in Nigeria. He said: “This MoU officially brings the biggest pivot irrigation manufacturer in the world on board as a major partner in building irrigation infrastructure across Nigeria under the Irrigate Nigeria Programme, the flagship irrigation programme of this administration.” He explained that beyond developing irrigation infrastructure, Valmont had agreed to work with NASENI to establish a local production facility for irrigation equipment. “Just as importantly, this partnership comes with the transfer of know-how and capacity building for Nigerians, which is precisely what technology transfer is all about,” he added. The agreement also provides for a pilot irrigation programme covering 40,000 hectares in Adamawa State. The project will be implemented in collaboration with the Nigeria Incentive-Based Risk Sharing System for Agricultural Lending (NIRSAL) and the National Agricultural Development Fund (NADF). While PICTT will lead the overall implementation of the programme, NASENI will drive the adoption and domestication of the technology. The partnership is also expected to create opportunities for collaboration with the University of Nebraska and the Robert B. Daugherty Water for Food Global Institute on sustainable irrigation systems and water resource management. Muhammed said key stakeholders had already expressed interest in expanding irrigation infrastructure through the partnership, describing the development as a vote of confidence in the programme. Officials said the agreement would help improve agricultural productivity, strengthen national food security and promote the sustainable management of water resources in line with the Federal Government’s agricultural transformation agenda. item.title: Troops rescue 18 abducted children, hunt for four others in Kaduna
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of the Nigerian Army under Operation Fansan Yamma have rescued 18 children abducted by suspected terrorists in Kaduna State, while intensifying efforts to secure the release of four others still held by the fleeing kidnappers. The children, members of the Boys’ and Girls’ Brigade, were reportedly abducted early Sunday, November 22, 2026, while participating in a morning group road walk at Mother-Cat Community in the Kachia/Kajuru general area of the state. Confirming the rescue in a statement on Sunday night, the Acting Director, Army Public Relations, Colonel Appolonia Anele, said troops of the 1 Division Nigerian Army, operating under Sector 1 of Operation Fansan Yamma, launched a rescue operation shortly after receiving a distress call. Anele said troops of Sub-Sector 5 immediately mobilised and pursued the abductors through surrounding bushes, advancing towards Rehina Riverside, where some of the children were found abandoned by the fleeing criminals. She said the troops sustained the pursuit along the river line, rescuing additional victims and bringing the number of recovered children to 18. According to the Army, sustained military pressure forced the abductors to abandon the children as they fled deeper into the surrounding forest. The statement added that troops had extended their search operations along the Ankwa–Kabode–Pachi link road and towards the Awon and Akwondo general areas to locate the remaining four children and apprehend those responsible for the abduction. The Army assured the families of the victims and the general public of its commitment to rescuing all the abducted children. It also said troops would sustain offensive operations and intelligence-led patrols to protect vulnerable communities and prevent further attacks. The military urged residents to remain vigilant and provide timely and credible information to security agencies to support the ongoing search-and-rescue operations and facilitate the arrest of the perpetrators. The post Troops rescue 18 abducted children, hunt for four others in Kaduna appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Laser Focus at the Top of the World
item.description: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory Laser Focus at the Top of the… Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search The Ny-Ålesund Geodetic Observatory is located on the west coast of Spitsbergen, an island in Norway’s Svalbard archipelago, shown in this image acquired with the OLI (Operational Land Imager) on Landsat 9 on July 30, 2026. NASA Earth Observatory/Lauren Dauphin More than 60 years ago, scientists at NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center aimed a laser skyward and fired a pulse of light at an orbiting satellite equipped with special reflectors. By measuring the time it took for the light to return, they demonstrated a new, more precise method for tracking satellites. Since then, satellite laser ranging (SLR) has grown more precise and more widely used. The technique now underpins many aspects of Earth observation, such as validating satellite orbits and mapping subtle changes to Earth’s surface. Pioneered at the Goddard Optical Research Facility—now the Goddard Geophysical and Astronomical Observatory —laser ranging is performed at more than 40 stations worldwide. In 2026, the next generation of SLR, developed by NASA scientists and tested at Goddard, began to come online. On October 12, a faster, even more precise SLR system officially debuted at the Ny-Ålesund Geodetic Observatory in Svalbard, Norway, operated by the Norwegian Mapping Authority, a NASA partner. The observatory’s remote location in the Arctic archipelago is shown in this image, acquired with the OLI (Operational Land Imager) on Landsat 9 in July 2026. It is the first NASA next-generation SLR system in operation and the northernmost SLR facility on Earth. While the systems developed decades ago have been “workhorses” of the global laser tracking network, their age and the growing number of satellites have necessitated updates, said Stephen Merkowitz, project manager for NASA’s Space Geodesy Project . “We wanted newer systems that could track more objects, and track them more accurately and precisely,” he said. The Space Geodesy Satellite Laser Ranging system fires at the Ny-Ålesund Geodetic Observatory in Svalbard, Norway, against a backdrop of aurora borealis on October 7, 2026. NASA/Julie Horvath (KBR) Years of development, testing, and careful calibration produced the Space Geodesy Satellite Laser Ranging system now running at Ny-Ålesund. Among its features are lasers that can fire pulses thousands of times per second, up from tens of times per second, and sensors that can detect single photons, meaning that less light needs to be reflected back from a satellite. item.title: GAS: Domestic market gets 41.3% as Nigeria’s supply averages 4.95bcf/d in 10 months
item.description: •LPG retail price rises 12.5% to N1,800 per kg •Make domestic market attractive to secure adequate supply — NALPGAM By Udeme Akpan Despite Nigeria’s 215.19 trillion cubic feet (Tcf) of proven natural gas reserves, the domestic market received an average of 2.04 billion cubic feet per day (bcf/d), representing 41.3 per cent of the country’s total supply of 4.95 bcf/d in the first 10 months of 2026. The Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority, NMDPRA, disclosed this in its latest report obtained by Vanguard. The report showed that the Nigeria LNG Limited, NLNG, received the remaining 58.7 per cent, averaging 2.91 bcf/d. In October, total average daily gas supply rose by 2.7 per cent to 4.951 bcf/d, from 4.822 bcf/d in September. Domestic supply increased by 2.3 per cent to 2.113 bcf/d, while deliveries to NLNG grew by three per cent to 2.838 bcf/d. April recorded the highest average daily supply during the 10-month period at 5.141 bcf/d, comprising 2.01 bcf/d for domestic market and 3.13 bcf/d for NLNG. Gas supply to power plants increased by 10 per cent to 0.571 bcf/d in October. Deliveries to gas-based industries also rose, while supplies to commercial users declined. Supply to the Escravos Gas-to-Liquids facility fell by two per cent. Gas exports also strengthened. Average daily LNG exports increased by seven per cent to 52,721 metric tonnes per day, from 49,198 metric tonnes per day in September, while pipeline exports through the West African Gas Pipeline (WAGP) rose by 11 per cent to 0.149 bcf/d, from 0.134 bcf/d. LPG retail price rises 12.5% to ₦1,800 per kg Meanwhile, the average retail price of liquefied petroleum gas, LPG, also known as cooking gas, rose by 12.5 per cent to ₦1,800 per kilogramme in November 2026, from ₦1,600 in October. Checks by Vanguard attributed the increase largely to limited supply. The average depot price of LPG stood at ₦1,274 in the Daily Depot Price Intelligence Report for Friday, November 20, 2026. The report covered Lagos, Warri, Calabar and Port Harcourt but did not provide a regional breakdown of LPG prices. Make domestic market attractive to secure adequate supply — NALPGAM The Executive Secretary/Chief Executive Officer of the Nigerian Association of Liquefied Petroleum Gas Marketers, NALPGAM, Bassey Essien, told Vanguard in an interview that Nigeria must make its domestic gas market commercially attractive to secure adequate supplies. He said: “Gas exports generate foreign exchange, but the domestic market must also be commercially attractive enough to secure adequate supply. ‘’The solution is not to stop exports but to make the domestic market competitive enough to attract supply while preserving export earnings.” On Domestic Gas Delivery Obligation, DGDO, Essien noted that regulation alone could not guarantee physical deliveries without adequate infrastructure and effective payment systems. “The Domestic Gas Delivery Obligation, DGDO, requires producers to supply the local marke

item.title: President Tinubu does not need this falsehood
item.description: By Dele Sobowale Each time President Tinubu mentions $1 trillion economy by 2030, he reveals more than the politicians’ penchant for making promises they cannot keep. He brings into question his proclaimed economic qualification as an accounting graduate for a Chicago university. There is abundant evidence, provided by Tinubu himself, to call that assertion a deliberate lie. I have touched on some of them before; but, Tinubu, despite expert advice continues to campaign on a promise which can never be redeemed. Here again, the facts which Tinubu stubbornly ignores; because they don’t fit into the narratives of a desperate politician running for elections, will once more be presented. This time fresh evidence will be added from Tinubu’s campaign organization. POLITICS AND FALSEHOOD ARE INSEPRABLE “The great masses of the people ..will fall victims to a great lie than to a small one.” Adolf Hitler, 1899-1945, VANGUARD BOOK OF QUOTATIONS, VBQ p 130. Politicians, under the best of circumstances, would repeat the same falsehood in the hope that saying it long enough will make it true. And, when they fail, they never apologise to the people; they blame others. President Tinubu’s assertion that Nigeria’s economy can grow to $1 trillion by 2030 is the sort of thing Hitler was talking about. I have given Tinubu the benefit of doubt that he read accounting in an American university as an undergraduate. But, his insistence that the Nigerian economy, whose Gross Domestic Product, GDP, is estimated to reach $386.67 billion at the end of the year 2026 could reach $1 trillion in just four years, would have had first year students of any university wondering if that was a joke or something else not hilarious. The figures don’t add up. LIARS CAN FIGURE; FIGURES DON’T LIE “Every government is run by liars and nothing they say should be believed. I.F Stone, 1907-1989. US Journalist and Publisher. Stone was one of my favourite columnists during my ten years in the US. I read his articles as if preparing for an examination on the subject discussed. He always led with evidence. So, let us start with the Federal Governments own figures. President Tinubu has been going round the country telling Nigerians the Nigerian economy is set to grow by 4.5 per cent this year. That will be the best performance since 2014. It is admittedly very commendable but worse than Jonathan’s worst year. The FG is also promising 6 percent growth in 2027. Highly praise-worthy if achieved. For some reason, not too difficult to understand, Tinubu, a self-proclaimed accountant, as well as his mob of supporters, cannot seem to understand that you cannot grow $386.67 billion to $1 trillion at 6 per cent in four years. This is primary school arithmetic called compound interest calculations. It is repeated at freshman level in American universities. Has Tinubu forgotten it or is he just peddling the big lie for political gain? QUANTUM LEAPS OF OTHER VARIABLES NEEDED “Economics is not magic; at its bes

item.title: Google claims last week’s critical VMware bug was under attack in September
item.description: Google’s Mandiant unit has claimed that the critical flaw VMware last week revealed in its vCenter product was under attack by a China-linked threat actor which knew of the bug in July and exploited it in September. VMware revealed several flaws on November 19. The big nasty is CVE-2026-123890, which allows unauthorized access to vCenter, the management console for hosts and guest VMs. According to seven researchers from Google’s threat intelligence group (formerly Mandiant), a crew it calls ARMORY CASTLE that it suspects of having links to the People’s Republic of China exploited CVE-2026-123890 by first compromising remote access appliances from BeyondTrust. Google’s analysis suggests the crew uses that toehold to establish access to other Linux appliances before moving deeper into victims’ networks. If the crew finds vCenter, it deploys a custom malware tool called “BONESAW” designed to slice into the VMware product. In the incident Google observed, BONESAW let attackers “forge authentication tokens, bypass MFA, and impersonate any user.” The gang put that access to work by conducting an inventory of the victim’s VMware setup, scooping up data describing the ESXi file system, attached disks, and mounted Virtual Machine File System volumes. ARMORY CASTLE also added an SSH public key to the root account’s authorized keys, and “conducted further reconnaissance and data theft on the ESXi filesystem using the root account.” Google also found evidence of BONESAW being used in July, on a server an unidentified entity had patched against CVE-2026-59309 – another authentication bypass vulnerability in vCenter. And BONESAW was just one of five tools Google thinks ARMORY CASTLE created as part of its plan to attack vCenter. It also made webshells named SLIMSAVAGE and CAGEMATCH, a backdoor called BEARBONES, and a SAML utility called SAWSNAKE. “The use of three separate specialized sets of malware and two zero-days in the course of a single campaign indicates that there are significant resources supporting ARMORY CASTLE operations,” Google’s researchers wrote. “It also shows the extent of the threat actor’s operational commitment to compromise high priority targets.” Few targets are as juicy as vCenter, because it can literally give attackers access to thousands of virtual machines and the hosts they run on. Google hasn't said how many attacks is saw on vCenter using BONESAW. The Register asked VMware if it was aware of the September attack, if it took any measures to defend its customers at the time, and to share a timeline for disclosure and remediation of CVE-2026-123890. A spokesperson responded by pointing to VMware’s Q&A document and stating “In today's threat environment, customers should assume any publicly disclosed critical vulnerability can and will be exploited by threat actors under the right conditions and should apply the recommended patches immediately.” VMware has tried to make that easier by adding non-disruptive patching to several of it

item.title: $1 of GPT-5.1 tokens finds new ways around China’s Great Firewall
item.description: Researchers have found new ways to evade China’s Great Firewall after spending just $1 worth of tokens. That result appeared last week in a paper titled “CircumVolve: Automated Discovery of Censorship Evasion Strategies Using Large Language Models” presented at the Conference on Computer and Communications Security run by the Association for Computing Machinery’s Special Interest Group on Security, Audit and Control. Penned by six researchers from the University of Massachusetts Amherst, University of Colorado Boulder, and activist group the Great Firewall Report, the paper points out that finding holes in the Great Firewall is a laborious process – so just the kind of task worth handing to AI. The authors came up with a tool they call “CircumVolve” and describe as “a system for automated discovery of censorship circumvention strategies across the full network stack.” “CircumVolve combines LLM code generation with iterative feedback-driven evaluation to produce verifiable and deployable evasion techniques,” they wrote. “CircumVolve models different censorship techniques as discrete scenarios, each capturing the specific context, protocol constraints, and blocking mechanisms of real-world censors. Within each scenario, evasion strategies are represented as executable Python programs that implement packet and protocol manipulations — from rewriting TCP/IP header fields, to crafting DNS queries that exploit parser ambiguities, to modifying the internal structure of encrypted QUIC Initial packets — while maintaining protocol correctness within tolerable bounds or strategically violating it when beneficial.” The authors tested CircumVolve on simulated censorship tools used by China, Iran, Pakistan, and Kazakhstan, and on virtual private servers deployed on clouds in those countries. Those tests found the median API cost to the first successful evasion was less than $1 in token expenditure costs when using GPT-5.1. The authors acknowledge that operators of censorship infrastructure might be able to observe CircumVolve at work, but feel its relatively small payloads – 80 KB of outgoing and 150 KB of incoming traffic – and 25-45-second pauses between tests might see it fly under the radar. “CircumVolve represents a first step in leveraging LLMs to accelerate the censorship-circumvention lifecycle,” the authors wrote. “By automating the labor-intensive tasks of protocol analysis, implementation, and testing, AI-driven approaches make studying circumvention capabilities far more accessible to the comparatively under-resourced Internet freedom community [and] demonstrates how AI-assisted systems can narrow the resource gap between Internet freedom advocates and well-funded censoring states.” Lenovo finally cracks monster datacenter profits Ever since acquiring IBM’s x86 server business in 2014, Chinese hardware giant Lenovo has struggled to turn a profit from datacenter sales, even as it expanded its business into storage, networking, and selling to hypersc

item.title: Ariane 6 launch of 36 Amazon Leo satellites postponed due to a technical issue
item.description: null Amazon's first satellite launch since a rocket failure doomed 40 of its spacecraft has been postponed due to a technical issue. An Ariane 6 rocket carrying 36 satellites for the Amazon Leo constellation was scheduled to lift off from Europe's Spaceport in Kourou, French Guiana, on Monday (Nov. 23). However, the countdown was halted following a technical issue affecting the rocket's ground support systems, according to Arianespace . The countdown was stopped before the removal of the mobile gantry, with Arianespace confirming that the rocket and its satellite payload remain safe and stable. Technical teams are now assessing the issue, with the next launch opportunity no earlier than Tuesday (Nov. 24). The launch will be streamed live here at Space.com, courtesy of Arianespace, once a new launch date and time have been confirmed. Amazon Leo, so named because it will operate in low Earth orbit , will compete with SpaceX's Starlink internet constellation, which currently consists of more than 11,000 operational spacecraft. Amazon's network will eventually have more than 3,200 satellites, but just 400 or so have reached orbit to date. Another 40 were supposed to be delivered on Nov. 15, but they were lost after their rocket ride, a United Launch Alliance (ULA) Vulcan Centaur , suffered a problem shortly after launch. Ariane 6 and Vulcan Centaur aren't the only rockets Amazon is depending on to build its broadband constellation. Jeff Bezos' company has also booked rides on ULA's Atlas V rocket, Blue Origin's New Glenn and SpaceX's Falcon 9 . Vulcan will be grounded for a while as ULA investigates the Nov. 15 failure and works to fix whatever caused it. And New Glenn hasn't flown since April, when the rocket failed to deliver AST SpaceMobile's BlueBird 7 satellite to the proper orbit. New Glenn's return to flight was further complicated on May 28, when the rocket exploded during a routine prelaunch test. The Ariane 6, the successor to Arianespace's Ariane 5 heavy lifter, debuted in July 2024 and has nine launches under its belt to date. All of them have been successful except that maiden mission, which was a partial failure. The upcoming mission will be the fourth Amazon Leo flight for the Ariane 6, following launches in February, April and June of this year. Editor's note: This article was updated at 5:30 a.m. EST on Nov. 23 to reflect the postponement of the Ariane 6 launch following a technical issue affecting the rocket's ground support systems. The next launch opportunity is no earlier than Nov. 24, according to Arianespace.

item.title: 65 Years of Human Spaceflight at NASA Johnson
item.description: 7 Min Read 65 Years of Human Spaceflight at NASA Johnson NASA astronaut Randy Bresnik, ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Luca Parmitano, former NASA astronaut Russell “Rusty” Schweickart, and NASA astronauts Frank Rubio and Bob Hines appear onstage at the Artemis Celebration Gala at the Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex in Merritt Island, Florida, on Nov. 6, 2026. Credits: Purpose Entertainment/Shanna Lockwood Employees and guests of NASA’s Johnson Space Center celebrate the center’s 65th anniversary at the Lunar Receiving Park in Houston on Nov. 19, 2026. NASA/Robert Markowitz For 65 years, NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston has helped shape human spaceflight, from the Gemini missions that demonstrated rendezvous and docking techniques needed for Apollo to the research conducted aboard the International Space Station, which has supported a continuous human presence for more than 26 years. Today, Johnson teams are preparing crews and systems for NASA’s next chapter: returning astronauts to the lunar surface and building the capabilities needed for a long-term human presence at the Moon. Across those missions, generations of flight controllers, engineers, scientists, instructors, medical specialists, and other experts have helped crews live and work beyond Earth. Johnson is home to NASA’s Orion and Moon Base programs, and its teams continue to support space station operations, astronaut training, spacecraft development, mission operations, and human health. Mercury and Gemini: Preparing for Apollo When the Manned Spacecraft Center officially opened on Nov. 1, 1961, NASA had already flown two suborbital Mercury missions, with the first orbital flight just months away. Most Project Mercury activities remained at Cape Canaveral in Florida to maintain continuity, but the new Project Gemini took up residence in Houston, housed in temporary leased facilities across the city while construction of the new Clear Lake campus continued. The new Mission Control Center became NASA’s primary flight control center in June 1965, with the Gemini IV mission that included the first American spacewalk. Houston became the nerve center for American human spaceflight, overseeing the remaining eight Gemini missions before transitioning to the Apollo program. Following the tragic Apollo 1 fire in January 1967, managers, engineers, and astronauts at the Manned Spacecraft Center applied lessons learned to make the spacecraft safer and ensure the safety of its astronauts, resuming crewed missions in October 1968. Managers in Houston devised a daring plan to send Apollo 8 on a circumlunar flight. In December 1968, Apollo 8 made its historic trip around the Moon, and seven months later Apollo 11 astronauts Neil Armstrong and Edwin “Buzz” Aldrin landed on the lunar surface. Their first voice transmission back to Earth after their arrival began with the word “Houston.” Five more Moon landings completed the Apollo program and humanity’s first phase of lunar exploration
